scope: Standing rock-cut Kailasa Temple, Cave 16, Ellora, covering the monolithic sanctuary, Nandi pavilion, entrance gate, elephant plinth, detached shrines and rock court with its enclosing cliffs.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: The Indian State Party report gives a rock court 82 by 46 metres and a rear rock scarp 32 m high. It describes the low western gopuram, separate Nandi porch, flat-roofed sixteen-pillar mandapa, Dravidian tower, two pillars, elephants, and detached shrines.
The Archaeological Survey of India identifies the surviving Cave 16 as the major monolithic Kailasa temple and connects it with Krishna I.
Government architectural training documentation gives the main body approximately 46 by 30 m, lofty 8 m plinth and approximately 31 m main tower.
